test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 22 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The distance between two stations A and B is 420 km. A train starts from A at 3 p.m. and travels towards B at a speed of 60 km/h. Another train starts from B at 4 p.m. and travels towards A at a speed of 30 km/h. At what time do they meet?
solution:
**Given:**

Distance between two stations A and B = 420 km.

Speed of the train starting from A = 60 km/h.

Speed of the train starting from B = 30 km/h.

Train from A starts at 3 p.m.

Train from B starts at 4 p.m.

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed of two trains moving towards each other = Speed of train 1 + Speed of train 2

Time = Distance / Relative speed

**Calculation:**

Train from A travels for 1 hour before the train from B starts.

Distance covered by train from A in 1 hour = 60 km/h × 1 h = 60 km

Remaining distance = 420 km - 60 km = 360 km

Relative speed of both trains = 60 km/h + 30 km/h = 90 km/h

Time taken to cover the remaining distance:

⇒ Time = 360 km / 90 km/h

⇒ Time = 4 hours

Trains meet 4 hours after 4 p.m.

⇒ 4 p.m. + 4 hours = 8 p.m.

**The trains meet at 8 p.m.**
